findings.claim: Partially closed. App writers and the trusted B4 consumer are now explicit, but the owner-generation equality rule does not enforce owner-only reactivation. After owner activation enabled:7, a delegated writer can set off and then restore enabled:7. The latest owner record is still generation 7, so the stated necessary-and-sufficient predicate accepts again without a new owner decision. No durable revocation/latch invalidates generation 7 when the variable changes. An off/on sequence between consumer reads is also invisible. This is a demonstrated wrong-gate path, hence P1 in this round.

evidence.observed: Enablement requires the latest OWNER activation record and matching variable value/generation. The text asserts that writers can only disable, but specifies no state transition that revokes that activation on disablement.

rc=0. Executed model of the written predicate: enabled:7 -> off -> enabled:7 yields targeted_allowed=true,false,true while owner_generation remains 7. The first and last observations are indistinguishable to a consumer that missed the intermediate write. This is a plan counterexample, not a live GitHub mutation.

Variables:write permits supplying the replacement value, including restoring an old value; it has no off-only operation. The GET representation exposes current value/timestamps, not a revocation history. [GitHub variable API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/variables#update-a-repository-variable).

findings.suggested_fix: In A+1/B4 and Q9, specify a trusted revocation mechanism that survives consumer restarts and cannot be undone by a variable writer. Either make disablement irrevocably consume an activation generation through a trusted durable control record, or restrict direct writes and provide an enforced off-only path. Do not rely solely on value equality or a consumer remembering an observed off value. Acceptance must reject delegated off/on replay, including between reads and after restart, and accept reactivation only after a fresh owner authorization. Freeze the resulting authority/state/write-set changes in B4 before PR3; preserve full-on-unknown and the existing PR1 contract.

findings.claim: The paired design fixes R4-14's before/after confounding, but its minimum acceptance is five pairs on one shard. That does not establish the <=5% overhead condition for the eight-shard G5 workload. No representative-shard justification, cross-shard coverage, weighting or restriction of the conclusion to the sampled shard is required. A compliant single-shard measurement can approve instrumentation whose aggregate overhead exceeds the limit.

evidence.observed: A+5 requires >=5 paired repeats on one shard, then applies the keep/remove decision to the instrumentation. Frozen PR1 instruments all eight shards; its outcome-parity acceptance covers all eight, but supplies no representativeness guarantee for a future one-shard timing sample.

rc=0. Deterministic heterogeneous-shard witness: all eight off-times=100 s; on-times=[100,120,120,120,120,120,120,120] s. Five identical pairs on shard 0 estimate 0% and pass, while total time rises 800->940 s, or 17.5%. Controlled homogeneous 0%,4%,20% cases estimate correctly, isolating coverage from the already-fixed pairing problem. Synthetic timings, not production measurements.

findings.suggested_fix: Define A+5's workload and percentage estimator explicitly. Cover all affected shards/modes with paired measurements, or preregister and justify a representative sampling/weighting scheme before inspecting results; otherwise report only the sampled shard and leave the global threshold unmeasured. Add the heterogeneous-shard witness alongside the known-overhead fixture. Assign measurement and any sampling change to PR3 or a successor without changing PR1, and revise the measurement budget for the chosen coverage rather than silently adding CI runs.
